# Produce blog drafts with Slack & Airtable

**Pattern:** Content Generation · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers blog-posts work end to end across Slack and Airtable.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Hourly Schedule
2. Keep Valid Drafts
3. Frame the Assignment
4. Coordinator Agent
5. OpenAI Chat Model
6. Research Specialist (Sub-workflow)
7. Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow)
8. Review Specialist (Sub-workflow)
9. Enforce Result Schema
10. Unpack Sections
11. Persist Deliverable to Airtable
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Tag Pipeline Metadata
14. Cap Batch Volume
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
17. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing blog-posts work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Hourly Schedule → Keep Valid Drafts → Frame the Assignment → Coordinator Agent → OpenAI Chat Model → Research Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Draft Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Review Specialist (Sub-workflow) → Enforce Result Schema → Unpack Sections → Persist Deliverable to Airtable → Save Execution Metadata → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Airtable aligned by hand for blog posts
- Blog posts work that needs a judgement call per item before it reaches Slack
- Blog posts work where "Keep Valid Drafts" is still a manual step before Slack
- Blog posts work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Airtable in step for blog posts, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Slack or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this blog-posts build
- Every blog-posts run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack
- The blog-posts AI step is isolated from Slack, so models swap without touching the other 19 nodes
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 19 nodes for blog posts before wiring Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The Coordinator Agent never does the specialist work itself — each specialist is delegated to its own sub-workflow via a Workflow Tool, so every specialist stays single-responsibility and testable in isolation instead of one giant prompt trying to do everything. An output parser forces the final answer into JSON so downstream nodes can rely on the shape instead of parsing free text.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Add a third specialist tool and update the system message to explain when the agent should reach for it.
2. Loosen or tighten the JSON schema on the output parser and see how the agent's final answer shape changes.
3. Replace one placeholder Workflow Tool with a real n8n sub-workflow and measure the round-trip latency.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your blog posts process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole blog-posts payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
